content:
Hello everyone,
Me and my team are planning to formalize the definition and properties of Covering Dimension of a Topological space. I found that the definition and its properties are missing in the mathlib4 library. The covering dimension is ≤n if for every open cover of the topological space X, you have a refinement of the cover (means a finer open cover with sets being subset of some set in the former collection) of order ≤n+1. I think this would be a great addition to the library. Has anyone got any idea (or) suggestions on it?

Thank you!

We are starting to work on formalizing the covering dimension of topological spaces and any guidance in this process would be really helpful. We are following the standard notations for the same.
Do you think that it would be a great addition to the mathlib4 library?
What are the things that I should keep in mind before a PR?

This list is surely non-exhaustive.

  1. Be sure to use existing API, e.g. docs#TopologicalSpace.IsOpenCover
  2. Avoid an extra universe parameter creeping into the type by following the pattern in docs#ParacompactSpace.
  3. You'll need to follow up the above by providing a lemma that you can have a different universe for the index set.
  4. Write very few definitions and as many basic lemmas as you can.
  5. Keep the initial PR to a reasonable size, say, under 200 lines. There can always be more after the first one.
Thank you for your guidance. I was not able to understand the points numbered 2 and 3. Do you mean to use less universal declarations and focus on local declarations? @Jireh Loreaux
No. Try reading the docstring forParacompactSpace. If it still doesn't make sense, ask again here and I'll provide more detail.

Raghunath J V said:

Thank you for your guidance. I was not able to understand the points numbered 2 and 3. Do you mean to use less universal declarations and focus on local declarations? Jireh Loreaux

He is referring to 'universes' in the 'Sort/Type' universe sense, and the docstring meaning here docs#ParacompactSpace ( as linked above ) .

The universe being fixed at some v throughout is in contrast to definitions you may see using Type*. In this case it is talking about a design choice regarding the desire to first index sets of a type in v using another type in the same universe. It can be a bit of a specific topic for a beginner, so feel free to post in #new members asking other things about it as well.

A lot more can be said as to why you'd do choose one implementation detail over another, why it matters, etc. , since using the one with one universe would be essentially the same as a polymorphic version application .{v,v} , and there are ways to move certain definitions between universes in order to potentially adapt to either scenario.

For self-learning you can often find more information about the justifications in the PR defining it, like here (includes a small bit about adaptation toType*):
https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib3/pull/6395#discussion_r584737594 ( expand the first review comment by Eric to see it if that link doesn't work properly ).

(This is off topic here, but I'm puzzled by the definition of docs#ParacompactSpace : the definition of docs#ParacompactSpace.locallyFinite_refinement postulates an index type β for the locally finite refinement which belongs to the same universe as the type α indexing the initial refinement. Imagine one is able to prove the assumption with a β that belongs to another universe — then one should need to apply a variant of docs#ParacompactSpace.precise_refinement to conclude that the space is actually paracompact. Am I missing something?)

The definition has to be formulated this way, because it shouldn't depend on another irrelevant universe. What we could (should?) do is have a theorem with another universe saying that, if you're able to prove the property using an index set in this other universe, then the space is paracompact wrt our current definition.

My question was indeed about whether Mathlib “could” or “should” have this additional lemma. (In fact, all open covers fundamentally reduce to objects in Set (Set X) so this shouldn't be a serious issue.

I think it would be better if we completely removed the quantifying over types in the definition, so removing the∀ (α : Type v) and ∃ (β : Type v), and replacing them with quantifying over Set (Set X) instead, so the universes are a non-issue.

The universes are already a non-issue as all these definitions are equivalent. As to whether we need the various lemmas saying that these definitions are equivalent, it's probably a good idea. I think they will show up naturally if anyone needs them, and otherwise it's not clear they're needed.

Yes: if you define paracompactness in terms of open cover(ing)s self-indexed as in Set (Set X), you put some burden on the users. There are 4 or 5 instances of docs#ParacompactSpace, so as long as nobody needed the property after having proved paracompactness by switching to a larger universe, this is not a urgent task.

Antoine Chambert-Loir said:

Yes: if you define paracompactness in terms of open cover(ing)s self-indexed as in Set (Set X), you put some burden on the users.

I don't understand. How is this burden any different from the burden you get from defining it in terms of covers indexed by Type v?

Paracompactness involves two covers, one as an input, and another one as output: the definition is more useful for users if the input allows more general types and the output is restricted; on the other hand, defining a paracompact space is easier if the input allows to input a restricted type and provide a general one as output.
but, surely there won't be any burden on the users as they can just use docs#presice_refinement (which should probably be namespaced)
Yes, in this case, the question is for defining a paracompact space.
